subject: Pricing follow-up: target $/1M token benchmarking vs OpenAI/Anthropic

Subject: Follow-up & pricing benchmarking (post-demo)

Hi Alicia / Tom — great to meet you earlier. Quick recap from our call and next steps so we stay aligned:

- Key asks I captured: monthly active inference volume (tokens), target latency for user-facing features, and target $/1M tokens you want to hit for vendor selection.
- You mentioned 150M tokens/month (approx) for generation workloads during steady state and a budget range you'd like to keep < $10/1M tokens if possible. Please confirm if I got that right.

Next steps I propose:
1) Confirm monthly token envelope (min / expected / max).
2) I'll share a short benchmarking summary comparing Redwood hosted, Dedicated, and typical managed hosts (OpenAI/Anthropic) on $/1M token economics and what drives those costs (batching, KV cache hit rate, quantization). See attached stub: redwood-pricing-benchmark-v1.pdf.
3) If numbers look good, we can set up a 2-week proof-of-concept (benchmark run) for the most common prompt sets — this will give concrete per-token effective costs.

A couple of notes on what drives unit economics: sequence length distribution matters (short chat tokens vs long-document summarization), prompt engineering to reduce prefix tokens, and caching/continuation ratio. If you can share a small sample set (anonymized), our SEs can run a quick cost model in the spreadsheet I'll attach.

Can you confirm:
- Final expected monthly tokens (150M ok as expected?),
- Target $/1M tokens (you said below $10 — is there a firm target?),
- Any procurement timing constraints?

Thanks — I'll loop Marissa/Finance for commercials once we have the clear volume/budget.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz

Hi Vanessa — thanks for the recap and for the quick demo. Confirming details from our side:

- Volume: our initial target for generative chat is ~150M tokens/month in Q1 after rollout; peak could reach 250M in promotional campaigns.
- Target price: procurement is pushing for something <= $8/1M tokens for generation. Lower is obviously preferred.
- Other considerations: data residency (US only) and SOC2 evidence (we'll want the questionnaire).

We've been running pilots with OpenAI and Anthropic and saw per-million-token software costs in the high teens for generation (after accounting for pricing tiers) which is higher than our target. We're evaluating managed-host partners that can bring closer to the <$10/1M ballpark.

Procurement note: we'll need a formal SOW and indicative pricing to share with legal/finance. If you can include committed throughput options (burst + reserved) and how pricing scales with a 12-month commit, that would be helpful.

Alicia Gomez
Head of ML Platforms, Acme Corp

Hi Alicia — thanks for confirming and for the candid target. Quick preliminary benchmarking notes to help frame options (high-level; final numbers depend on prompt mix and cache hit-rate):

- OpenAI (public API, generation) — rough market spot: ~$18-22 per 1M tokens for LLM generation at production scales (can vary by model and compression). This is often higher due to lack of caching and per-request penalties for session context.
- Anthropic (public API) — similar band to OpenAI, in the high teens per 1M tokens for many use-cases.
- Open-model hosts / self-hosted (GPU-backed with quantization) — raw infra cost can drop to ~$4-10/1M tokens depending on batching, sequence length, and quantization level; requires engineering overhead or dedicated partner.
- Redwood Hosted — for your volume (150M+/month) we can be in the ~$7-9/1M tokens range on hosted plans with good batching and caching.
- Redwood Dedicated / Reserved capacity — with a 12-month commit + reserved GPU pools we can go lower: target pricing in the $3.5-5.0/1M tokens band depending on model family and KV cache behavior. This typically requires a committed throughput SLA and a short benchmarking pilot to validate assumptions.

Notes on delta vs OpenAI/Anthropic:
- Biggest gaps come from caching and ability to run optimized kernels (quantized models) + lower service margin on reserved infra.
- If your average prompt length is low and you get strong prefix cache hits (e.g., lots of short message completions), effective $/1M drops materially.

I attached a short model that shows line-items (acme_token_modeling.xlsx) and a PDF summary (redwood-pricing-benchmark-v1.pdf) with the bands above. 

Proposed next steps:
1) We'll run a 7-14 day proof-of-concept on Redwood Hosted (no commit) to measure effective tokens/second, prefix cache hit, and real-world $/1M. This takes ~3 business days to set up.
2) If results are favorable we'll move to a Dedicated reserved proposal with a target commercial sheet (Marissa will draft).
3) Provide SOC2 + security docs to procurement (I'll CC our security team after you confirm).

If $8/1M is your procurement threshold, we should be able to show a path: hosted benchmark to prove effective costs and then commit-based Dedicated pricing to hit your long-term target.

Would you be open to starting the PoC the week of Nov 16?

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com

Attachments: acme_token_modeling.xlsx, redwood-pricing-benchmark-v1.pdf

Subject: Internal: ACME pricing guidance / next steps (RDW-2026-ACME-01)

Vanessa / Rishi — quick internal note before we lock the external SOW:

- Deal summary: ACME is ~150M tokens/month expected, target <= $8/1M tokens (procurement). They've run pilots with OpenAI/Anthropic and see high-teens $/1M.
- Recommendation: Offer a two-stage commercial approach:
  1) Short Hosted PoC (7-14d) to gather empirical effective $/1M. No long-term commit. SE to run prompt sets and capture cache hit rates.
  2) If PoC validates ~<$9/1M effective cost, propose a 12mo Reserved Dedicated agreement with tiered pricing: start at $6/1M with step-downs to $4/1M with 12mo commit + minimum throughput (to get to their $8 target and below).
- Commercial levers: commit term, minimum throughput, model family (quantized open models vs larger closed models), and support/SLA level.
- Risks: if prompt mix contains many long-document summarization requests, effective $/1M will be higher. Need sample prompt set ASAP.

Action items:
- Vanessa: ask ACME for anonymized prompt sample and confirm PoC kickoff week (Nov 16).
- Rishi: prep the PoC runbook and quick-cost tooling.
- Marissa (me): draft a commercial term sheet template with the tiered pricing and reserve a pricing band for legal/finance to review.

I'll be ready to jump on the customer call if they want contract-level details.

-Marissa Cole
Head of Sales Ops, Redwood Inference
